content.text: •Can appear in any part of the brain
(may be worse in the Am, awaken pt @ night, or positional), CN deficits, AMS chgs, neuro deficits, ataxia, vision chgs, weakness
HA, N/V, papilledema, ataxia, drowsiness, stupor
: generally form sacs of fluid (cystic), or may be enclosed w.in a cyst;
•post-op radiation if tumor cannot be completely removed; 90% 5y survival rate
•vomiting, HA, nausea, visual chgs (double vision), unsteady walking or clumsiness
•Ependymal cells line the ventricles & parts of the spinal column; 3
MC in children (mean age @ dx = 6yrs, 30% occur <3y)
chgs in mood, personality, or concentration; sz, balance/gait disturb, spinal cord compress sxs (back pain, loss of bladder/bowel control)
MC primary intraocular malig in childhood
in the tumor (RB1 = a tumor suppressor gene on chromosome 13)
: ← germline mut in the RB1 gene
(presence of abnorm white reflex instead of the norm red reflex)
F/U: retinoblastoma can be assoc w/ bone neoplasms (Osteosarcoma)
